who.value: Designer or engineer using the prototype kit

stage.value: Not a user journey stage; a component reference page

job.value: See the real @carousell/web-design components in one place

questions.title: The screen's job is clear from the first screen
questions.why: The 'Playground' tag, 'Web Design Playground' title and the one-line description say exactly what the page is.

questions.title: The action that does the job stands out most
questions.why: There is no single action; the page is a list of specimens (Typography, Buttons, Chips), which suits a reference page but gives no clear entry point.

questions.title: Every label says what happens when tapped
questions.why: Most specimens are labelled ('Title 1 — the largest headline', 'Disabled'), but one teal button shows only a loading glyph and the round '+' button has no label.

questions.title: No terms this user wouldn't know
questions.why: '@carousell/web-design' and 'components/design-system-web' are familiar to the kit's designer and engineer audience.

questions.title: Only asks what this user can decide at this stage
questions.why: No decisions are asked; it's view-only.

questions.title: Advanced detail is tucked away
questions.why: Every specimen is laid out flat with no grouping or collapse, which is expected for a kitchen sink but makes it long.

questions.title: Everything fits this stage and this user
questions.why: A shopper top nav ('Hi, Adele', cart, Sell) wraps a page whose audience is the design team, not a shopper.

questions.title: Little reading needed to act
questions.why: Specimen labels are short ('Large callout — 17px bold'); the only sentence is the description line.
